prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments. Elements: Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, receives station local-constraint notices, hosts primary routing policy point; each contact has readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit, maneuvers, navigation; sends visibility predictions and antenna pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility: processing, calibration, distribution staging; coordinates downlink allocation with Primary (nominal) and Backup (failover, lower routing preference, paths routinely tested) Processing Clusters. Network Control System (Lantern): authoritative WAN circuit status, path selection, maintenance windows; distributes station allocations, confirms antenna readiness, records contact start/end; vets timing alarms before forwarding to Spacecraft Operations Team. Long Term Archive: data, records, evidence; Primary Cluster-to-LTA transfers rate limited during contacts. User Services Portal: search, ordering, status. Mission Planning System: receives contact booking requests (service type, antenna preference, minimum elevation, data volume, priority class). Command Validation Gateway: pre-uplink check. Telemetry Ingest Service: receives telemetry, contact status/data-flow indicators; feeds ops, engineering, processing. Orbit Determination Engine: orbit knowledge, Doppler Residual Report per pass. Product Quality Service. Ground Network Manager (Juniper): antenna availability, conflict arbitration, issues Antenna Deicing Notice; pins critical paths pre-AOS; on latency breach checks carrier, routing, loss, queues, inspection delay before declaring mission-impacting condition; coordinates with Cybersecurity Desk before blocking traffic. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate) via protected access routers to MCC; Kiruna and Svalbard X-Band (high-rate downlink), dual WAN to PPF. Redundant diverse circuits link MCC, FDF, PPF, LTA. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team, Flight Dynamics Team (monitors timing quality), Payload Calibration Team, Cybersecurity Desk (sends Security Exception Ticket), station operators. Rules: routine contacts frozen at daily cut-off; contingency insertion needs justification; priority safety>timeliness>efficiency; X-band moved if precipitation cuts margin; routing: approved prefixes, authenticated neighbors, no changes during contacts, static backups, admin via unadvertised networks. New part:
S078: The North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna are normally assigned for command and low-rate telemetry contacts, while the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna support high-rate telemetry reception when the visibility geometry and data volume justify their use.
S079: The Network Control System provides the Mission Control Center with antenna status, link configuration, timing references, and routing readiness before each pass begins.
S080: The Telemetry Ingest Service accepts real-time frames, validates basic framing and time continuity, and records reception metadata needed for later operational review.
S081: The Telemetry Ingest Service produces the Pass Replay Packet after a contact when the received stream must be reconstructed for engineering review.
S082: During live operations, the Spacecraft Operations Team monitors spacecraft mode, power state, thermal margins, attitude indicators, command counters, onboard storage, and fault protection messages from the Mission Control Center consoles.
S083: Console displays emphasize deviations from expected state rather than raw parameter volume, because operators must identify safety trends while a contact is still available.
S084: The console lead is responsible for declaring pass status, authorizing planned command execution through the Command Validation Gateway, and pausing the activity when telemetry does not match the expected configuration.
S085: The telemetry engineer verifies reception quality, frame loss, latency, and stream continuity, and advises the console lead when degraded link conditions could affect command confidence.
S086: The spacecraft systems engineer interprets health telemetry, confirms that subsystem states remain within flight rules, and records any anomaly context needed by subsystem specialists.
S087: The Ground Network Manager remains accountable for antenna assignment, ground link availability, and coordination with site operations when weather, equipment status, or routing issues affect a contact.
S088: The Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking measurements and validated time tags from the contact to support orbit assessment at the Flight Dynamics Facility.
S089: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine state updates and provides the basis for predicting future visibility periods, maneuver planning constraints, and antenna pointing expectations.
S090: Pass reconstruction begins when the contact closes and combines command history, received telemetry timing, ground station status, and operator log entries into a single operational narrative.
S091: The reconstructed pass record is used to confirm whether planned objectives were completed, whether any onboard event occurred outside the timeline, and whether additional engineering analysis is required.
S092: The Payload Processing Facility is also known operationally as Forgehouse in console discussions and shift logs.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
